corrections.claim: federal_holidays: year 1968, note "Uniform Monday Holiday Act of 1968 set the Monday rules"; cited for "Federal law fixes Veterans Day on November 11, Thanksgiving on the fourth Thursday of November, and the King holiday on the third Monday of January."
corrections.problem: The 1968 act is the wrong anchor for two of the three dates. The 1968 Uniform Monday Holiday Act moved Veterans Day off November 11 to a Monday in October. A 1975 law (Pub. L. 94-97, effective 1978) moved it back to November 11. The King holiday was added in 1983 (Pub. L. 98-144). The fourth-Thursday Thanksgiving rule dates to 1941.
corrections.correct: Cite 5 U.S.C. 6103 as currently codified (as amended) with no single 1968 year. Or rewrite the note: "Thanksgiving fourth Thursday since 1941; Veterans Day returned to November 11 by Pub. L. 94-97 (1975); King holiday added by Pub. L. 98-144 (1983)."
corrections.evidence: Statutory history of 5 U.S.C. 6103 (reviewer knowledge).

corrections.claim: "...discussion-centered classrooms trace to the Harkness gift of 1930."
corrections.problem: This overstates the cultural origin. The 1930 gift founded Exeter's Harkness method, which the body claim states correctly.
